title: Acetaminophen (paracetamol) maximum dose
text: Acetaminophen (paracetamol): the maximum recommended dose for healthy adults is 4,000 mg per day, that is 4 grams in any 24 hours. Exceeding this can cause severe liver injury. Source: FDA prescribing information.

title: Ibuprofen in pregnancy
text: Ibuprofen and other NSAIDs should be avoided from about 20 weeks of pregnancy onward, because they can cause fetal kidney problems and premature closure of the ductus arteriosus. Source: FDA Drug Safety Communication.

title: Warfarin INR target
text: For most patients taking warfarin, including those with atrial fibrillation or venous thromboembolism, the target INR range is 2.0 to 3.0. Source: ACCP antithrombotic therapy guideline.

title: Aspirin and Reye's syndrome
text: Aspirin should not be given to children or teenagers who are recovering from a viral infection such as influenza or chickenpox, because of the risk of Reye's syndrome. Source: CDC.

title: Metformin and kidney function
text: Metformin is contraindicated in patients whose estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) is below 30 mL/min/1.73m2, because of the risk of lactic acidosis. Source: FDA prescribing information.

title: ACE inhibitors in pregnancy
text: ACE inhibitors such as lisinopril are contraindicated in pregnancy, because they can cause fetal injury and death, particularly in the second and third trimesters. Source: FDA label.

title: Penicillin allergy
text: Patients with a documented severe penicillin allergy should avoid other beta-lactam antibiotics unless cross-reactivity has been formally evaluated. Source: clinical allergy guideline.

title: Influenza vaccination
text: An annual influenza vaccine is recommended for everyone aged 6 months and older, with rare medical exceptions. Source: CDC ACIP recommendations.
